headline: 3 foreign nationals killed, 36 injured in attacks on two Saudi international airports
summary: Two international airports in Saudi Arabia were attacked on Wednesday and Thursday, resulting in the deaths of three foreign civilians and injuries to 36 others. Saudi Arabia blames Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels for the assaults.
details: Three foreign civilian nationals, including women, were killed and at least 36 others injured in attacks on two international airports in Saudi Arabia. The attacks occurred on Wednesday and Thursday local time.
The General Authority of Civil Aviation stated that two foreign women, one Moroccan and one Algerian, died in the attack on Abha International Airport. This assault also left 28 people injured.
Separately, one Sudanese foreign national was killed in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Eight people were injured in this incident, five of whom are Saudi citizens.

Saudi Arabia alleges that Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are responsible for these attacks. The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned the incidents, and the US Embassy in Riyadh issued a special travel warning for American citizens.

headline_marked: [[Mother testifies about son's death and threat]] at ICT, implicates top leaders in July uprising case
headline: Mother testifies about son's death and threat at ICT, implicates top leaders in July uprising case
summary: The mother of 14-year-old Emon, who was shot during the July mass uprising, gave her testimony at the International Crimes Tribunal-1, detailing his tragic death and the threats she received afterward. She accused former PM Sheikh Hasina and other leaders.
details: Kulsum Begum, mother of 14-year-old Emon, who was shot dead in Dhaka's Badda during the July mass uprising, testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-1. She recounted her son's tragic death and the threats she received after finding his body.

Emon left home on July 20, 2024, with friends Naim and Shahin, joining the movement at Tetultala intersection in North Badda. About half an hour later, Shahin informed Emon's elder brother Rajib that Emon had been shot. Kulsum Begum rushed to the scene with her husband and elder son, where she fainted upon seeing her son lying in a pool of blood.

Upon regaining consciousness, Kulsum Begum found herself at home, with her son's lifeless body outside. She described a small bullet hole at the back of his skull, damaged skin on his left cheek, and a bullet mark on his chest. An Awami League member then threatened her, stating, 'You have found the body, you cannot cry, or we will make the body disappear.'

Kulsum Begum also shared the difficulties faced during Emon's burial. Her elder son, Rajib, was denied a stretcher from a local mosque. They eventually secured a stretcher and a person to perform the ritual washing from another mosque.

After the Janaza prayer, they began their journey to Bhola with Emon's body in an ambulance around 11 PM. On the way, Awami League members and law enforcement officials obstructed them at three different locations. After much pleading, they were allowed to proceed, and Emon was finally buried in their ancestral village in Bhola the following day.

In her testimony at the tribunal, Kulsum Begum held former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader, Rashed Khan Menon, and Kamrul Islam responsible for her son's murder. She demanded justice for Emon.
Rashed Khan Menon and Kamrul Islam, who are accused in this case, are currently imprisoned.
